evidence: infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:75-78: blank/None/CHANGEME → returns empty, indistinguishable from a transient read error
fetch-secrets.sh MCP block: `add_mcp_record ... [ -z "${value}" ] && return 0` omits the record when value is blank, and the tokens file is `mv -f` overwritten each run
Contrast: required creds use get_param which fail-fast aborts (line 57-59) rather than silently degrading
dropped.finding: get_param_optional swallows all aws/IMDS errors ('2>/dev/null || true') and returns blank on ANY failure; because the MCP tokens file is ALWAYS rewritten from these values, a transient SSM read failure during a re-materialize silently OMITS a client's token_env record even though its SSM value is intact — quietly retiring a live client (idempotency/drift: same SSM state can yield different tokens files).
scenarios: An SSM throttle/timeout on one mcp-client-pat leaf during a re-materialize drops that client's record while other clients survive, silently 401-ing a previously-valid client after the next rebar-mcp restart

dropped.finding: A per-client bearer PAT rotation is a value-only SSM change with no git effect, so autodeploy no-ops and the OLD digest set stays live until an operator manually restarts rebar-mcp — a compromised/rotated PAT remains accepted for an unbounded, unenforced window (blast radius) with only runbook prose as the control.
scenarios: A leaked PAT is rotated in SSM but the operator forgets step 3 (restart); the retired token keeps authenticating indefinitely
